B200 SXM6 appears again at 6.79, 6.89, and 6.99 dollars, next to 104, 52, and 26 vCPUs. H100 SXM on those rows is 4.09, 4.19, and 4.29 dollars. An H100 PCIe row with 80 GB and 26 vCPUs is 3.29 dollars. A GH200 row with 96 GB is 2.29 dollars. Under the B200 section the page says the instances start at 6.69 dollars, and it says the part offers up to three times the training and fifteen times the inference of H100. It does not say how many tokens that hour produces.

...

A spot floor is not the on-demand rate. Nebius says the preemptible price can change as often as every fifteen minutes, that it stays at least one cent under the on-demand rate, and that the number on the documentation page is a minimum. The phrase is "from 0.79" or "from 0.99", not the charge a running job will see. The on-demand column is the figure a reader can compare next month without logging into a console.

An H100 hour has not moved in one smooth line, and the two rates on the chart are different offers. The SXM5 pay-as-you-go hour was $4.85 from November 2023 through July 2024, and $3.50 on 15 September 2024. The later NVLink hour was $2.95 from October 2025 through May 2026, $3.85 from 1 June 2026, and $4.50 from 1 October 2026. The months between September 2024 and November 2025 are left empty. A third quote, $2.118 for the GPU alone with the processor and memory billed beside it, is not drawn.

The useful update is the dated move on the Nebius page itself. From 1 October 2026 the on-demand H100 line goes from 3.85 to 4.50 dollars, the H200 line from 4.50 to 5.40, the B200 line from 7.15 to 8.50, and the B300 line from 7.85 to 9.50. Those four pairs are on one document, with the old rate left in place under a "before" heading. Lambda's instance rows do not carry a date. The 6.69 and 3.99 dollar figures are what that URL showed on 10 October 2026, and a revision should open the URL again rather than treat them as a contract.

results.title: RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99
highlights:
RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99

# RunPod’s Secure Cloud GPU Rates Have Risen: H100 SXM Now $3.99 an Hour, B200 $7.99, a Tracker Reports

October 10, 2026

Illustration.

A GPU price tracker, GPU Economy, says RunPod raised 12 of its 29 on-demand Secure Cloud GPU rates on 8 October 2026 [1]. RunPod’s pricing page now shows the higher prices [2]. RunPod made no announcement that we could find, so the timing and the old prices rest on the tracker.

## The new rates

RunPod sells two tiers, Secure Cloud and Community Cloud; on its listings the Community rates are lower. Prices are in US dollars per GPU per hour, on demand, meaning pay as you go. GPU Economy reports [1]:

| GPU | Before | Now | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.49 | $3.99 | +14.3% |
| H200 | $4.59 | $5.29 | +15.3% |
| B200 | $6.79 | $7.99 | +17.7% |
| B300 | $7.89 | $8.99 | +13.9% |

The H100, H200, B200 and B300 are Nvidia data-centre chips used to train and run AI models. The tracker says the 12 rises came “between our reads of October 8, 2026 at 15:41 and 16:41 UTC”, which is 16:41 and 17:41 in London. It also computes that one H100 SXM running for a 730-hour month went from $2,547.70 to $2,912.70.

## What did not change

The tracker says “None of the 35 Community Cloud on-demand rates changed in the same read”: the H100 SXM there stayed at $2.69 and the B200 at $5.98 [1].

## What RunPod’s page shows

RunPod’s pricing page lists $3.99/hr for the H100 SXM, $7.99/hr for the B200, $5.29/hr for the H200 and $8.99/hr for the B300 [2]. But the page is labelled “Updated September 27, 2026”, which does not match the tracker’s 8 October timing. The page’s hidden structured data, the code search engines read, still lists the old Secure Cloud prices, such as $3.49 for the H100 SXM [2]. The tracker says it read RunPod’s public API, and that on 9 October the page’s own markup still carried $3.49 [1]. That fits what we see.

## What this does not show

- A RunPod announcement. We found none, and no reason for the rises.
- When RunPod made the change. The tracker reads hourly and gives a one-hour window.
- Other providers’ prices. This covers RunPod only.
- Every region or product. Serverless and cluster pricing are not covered.

results.title: Nvidia GPUs are everywhere. Here's how companies access them
highlights:
Key Points

- AI labs are spending tens of billions of dollars per year for Nvidia chips that run their models.
- The demand has led to the blossoming of an industry that hyperscalers once had to themselves, including lucrative one-off arrangements and asset-light strategies.
- Over 300 neoclouds now rent GPUs to businesses, according to a review from researcher SemiAnalysis, up 55% in under 11 months.

...

Customers can now shop around for access to the chips at the giant clouds from Amazon, Microsoft and Google, as well as at so-called neoclouds like CoreWeave. They can also go to various online marketplaces or even buy the costly hardware directly.

...

Industry research firm SemiAnalysis counted 323 Nvidia GPU providers as of September, up from 209 less than 11 months earlier.

...

## Flagship neoclouds

If the hyperscalers were adequate, neoclouds wouldn't be proliferating.

Modal, a startup operating virtual sandboxes where AI agents work independent of main IT environments, went from running on the hyperscalers to signing up with the major neoclouds, and now it uses 25 of them, said CEO Erik Bernhardsson. 

"You can get a few hundred GPUs or maybe a thousand, but at our scale, we needed way more GPUs," he said. 

The hyperscalers themselves are also chasing the neoclouds. Google and Microsoft have started tapping CoreWeave, even as they all compete with one another.

"Some of the hyperscalers have approached us about taking care of customers they're worried about because they don't have the ability to service those customers when they need it," said Marc Boroditsky, chief revenue officer of Nebius, a Netherlands-based neocloud with operations in the U.S.

Video generation startup Reactor uses GPUs through Nebius and hyperscalers, said CEO Alberto Taiuti. The location of data centers matters, he said, because Reactor wants user-created videos to show up right away.

...

The most visible neoclouds can require some upfront payment, and chips might not come online for months, because providers raise funding based on contracts and set up the data center equipment, Bernhardsson said.

It would be difficult for CoreWeave to turn over 10,000 GPUs to a new customer with one day's notice, said Chen Goldberg, an executive vice president. CoreWeave's near-term capacity remains essentially sold out, CEO Mike Intrator said on the company's August earnings call.

...

Specialist neoclouds can offer more flexibility than the larger GPU clouds, which often require upfront payments and long-term commitments. Some sell so-called bare-metal GPUs, which give customers more control but also require them to manage more of the technical work themselves. 

Companies using these smaller neoclouds share the same concerns: When can they get the GPUs, and at what price? Sunny Smith, co-founder and technology chief at Massed Compute, said customers are often willing to commit to capacity when they expect prices to rise.

...

The hourly spot price for an Nvidia B200 GPU has more than doubled since March, according to data from Ornn, a startup that maintains indexes.

Collaboration software maker Dropbox Add To Watchlist relies on GPUs in its data centers, CEO Ashraf Alkarmi said.

results.title: AWS just raised reserved GPU prices again. This is the fourth hike this year. | Spheron Network
highlights:
AWS just raised reserved GPU prices again. This is the fourth hike this year.

Effective Oct 7, AWS Capacity Block rates climb to $5.97/hr for H100 (up from $5.19) and $16.15/hr for B300. That puts H100 and B300 on AWS up 40 to 75% since January.

Our marketplace rate for H100 is still $2.01/hr. For B300 it is $5.85/hr. Neither has moved all year.

Our H100 rate is 66% below AWS's new rate, and our B300 rate is 64% below AWS's new rate, for the same chip on the same day. Spheron is a marketplace, not a single cloud, so prices do not quietly creep up every quarter.

results.title: GPU 클라우드 323곳 집계…8개월 새 209곳서 늘어 | 토큰포스트
highlights:
기업의 엔비디아 GPU 조달 경로가 대형 클라우드에서 전문 GPU 클라우드와 개별 계약, 자체 데이터센터로 넓어졌다. GPU 클라우드 제공업체는 8개월 사이 209곳에서 323곳으로 늘었지만, 업체 수가 실제로 빌릴 수 있는 물량을 뜻하지는 않는다.

세미애널리시스(SemiAnalysis)는 9월 23일 공개한 ‘ClusterMAX 3.0’ 요약에서 GPU 클라우드 제공업체가 323곳이라고 밝혔다. 이전 집계 209곳보다 늘어난 수치다. 보고서는 유료 구독 콘텐츠로, 업체별 목록과 전체 산정 기준은 공개 요약에 담기지 않았다.

기업은 아마존웹서비스(AWS), 마이크로소프트 애저, 구글 클라우드 같은 대형 사업자를 먼저 검토할 수 있다. 이들 서비스는 기존 기업용 서비스와 보안·운영 체계를 함께 제공한다. CNBC는 대형 클라우드에서 필요한 시점에 충분한 GPU를 확보하기 어려운 사례와 대안으로 떠오른 전문 GPU 클라우드를 소개했다.

코어위브(CoreWeave)와 네비우스(Nebius) 같은 네오클라우드는 GPU 연산 자원 임대에 집중한다. CNBC는 AI 에이전트 개발사 모달(Modal)이 여러 네오클라우드를 이용한다고 전했다. 에릭 베른하르드손(Eric Bernhardsson) 모달 CEO는 회사 규모에 필요한 GPU를 기존 대형 클라우드만으로 확보하기 어려웠다고 말했다.

네오클라우드도 즉시 이용 가능한 GPU를 항상 보장하지는 않는다. CNBC는 일부 대형 사업자의 GPU가 계약과 데이터센터 구축 이후 수개월이 지나야 가동될 수 있다고 전했다. 코어위브의 마이크 인트라토(Mike Intrator) CEO도 8월 실적 발표에서 단기 공급 능력이 사실상 매진 상태라고 말했다.

...

임대료 지수도 공급 여건을 살필 자료 가운데 하나다. 오른(Ornn)은 10월 9일 엔비디아 B200 임대료 지수가 GPU·시간당 7.46달러(약 1만원)였다고 공개했다. 이 지수는 개별 업체의 공시 가격이 아니라 거래 가격을 가중 평균한 값이다.

오른 지수에서 B200 임대료는 30일 기준 9.4% 올랐지만, 7일 기준으로는 5.6% 내렸다. 기간에 따라 지수의 방향이 달라 단일 시점 수치만으로 임대료 흐름을 단정하기 어렵다. 오른은 B200 거래 기반 임대료 지수를 공개하고 있다.

GPU 조달 경로가 늘어난 사실은 확인되지만, 업체 수 증가만으로 공급량이나 가격 경쟁이 개선됐다고 볼 수는 없다. 세미애널리시스의 공개 집계는 제공업체 수를 다루며, 업체별 가용 용량과 계약 조건은 보여주지 않는다.

results.title: Bitdeer first read October 10, 2026: GB200 $6.94, H100 SXM $2.36
highlights:
The figure$2.36 Bitdeer AI, H100 SXM, 1 GPU, on demand, 1-year and 3-year terms, advertised from · on demand $2.36, 1 year $2.0768, 3 years $1.7936 per GPU-hour · read Oct 11, 05:39 UTC · source · live page

Every figure below is a reading this site published - a rate read on a provider's own page, or a value of the index computed from such rates - listed with its source under the text and frozen as of that day: prices move, and a dated piece says what was true on its date. The live tables are linked beside each figure.

We read Bitdeer AI’s GPU price list for the first time at 16:39 UTC on October 10, 2026. In our read of 05:39 UTC on October 11 it gave twelve rates on four NVIDIA cards. On demand, a GB200 NVL72 GPU was $6.941 an hour, the lowest of the 6 GB200 rate cards on our GB200 page, where the median was $13.25. An H100 SXM was $2.36 an hour, third from the bottom of 33 H100 SXM rate cards, against a median of $3.55.

...

Bitdeer’s pricing page prints one table, “GPU Model Pricing”, with a row per size and three columns per row: on demand, a 1-year term and a 3-year term, all in US dollars per hour for the whole size. Every figure on it is printed as “from”, and the page says nothing about what is added on top, so our pages tag all twelve rates “advertised from” rather than as an instance price. We keep one quote per card and market, the size with the lowest price per GPU. For the GB200 that is a tray of 4 GPUs at $27.764 an hour, which is $27.764 ÷ 4 = $6.941 per GPU. For the B200 it is the 2-GPU size at $9.38 an hour, $9.38 ÷ 2 = $4.69 per GPU. The H100 SXM and the H200 are priced per single GPU.

## Against each card’s median

On demand, Bitdeer’s four rates sat below all four medians in the October 11 read. The GB200 at $6.941 was below the next rate card, GMI Cloud’s $8.00, and about half the $13.25 median: $6.941 ÷ $13.25 is 0.52. The H100 SXM at $2.36 was 33% under the $3.55 median ($2.36 ÷ $3.55 is 0.66). The H200 at $2.761 was fifth from the bottom of 45 H200 rate cards, where the median was $4.54. The B200 at $4.69 was fifth from the bottom of 32 B200 rate cards, where the median was $7.06. Each rank is counted on the same rate cards the page’s median is taken over, one per provider, the provider’s lowest on-demand rate.

...

Bitdeer is one of the providers that print a committed rate beside the on-demand one, and both terms are hourly figures on the page. For the H100 SXM, the 3-year rate of $1.7936 is $1.7936 ÷ $2.36 = 0.76 of the on-demand rate, 24% lower; the 1-year rate was $2.0768. For the H200 the terms were $2.5125 and $2.264 against $2.761 on demand. For the B200 they were $4.3617 and $4.0803 against $4.69. The widest gap was the GB200: $4.9975 on a 3-year term against $6.941 on demand, which is $4.9975 ÷ $6.941 = 0.72, 28% lower, with $6.0387 on a 1-year term. These rates are listed on our reserved page with every other committed rate we read. A committed rate is billed for the whole term; the figures above are what the table printed, not a quote for a contract.

Nothing here is forecast. This is the first day we read this page, so there is no earlier Bitdeer figure to compare with, and none of these rates is a change in Bitdeer’s prices: it is what the table showed when we started reading it.

results.title: AI Compute Cost Outlook: Quarterly Briefing · AgentFlare
highlights:
### Pricing is high at the hyperscalers, discounted elsewhere

As of early November, H100 on-demand pricing ranged from roughly $6.88 per GPU-hour at AWS to $11.06 at Google Cloud, versus approximately $3.90–$6.16 across major neoclouds. [5] H200 pricing reached $10.60 per hour on Google Cloud, while B200 capacity was generally available through flexible-start or committed products rather than standard on-demand listings. [4] 

The spread is economically material: hyperscaler list prices averaged nearly twice GPU-cloud medians across H100, H200, and B200 instances. [1] This creates a strong incentive for workload migration, capacity brokering, and multicloud arbitrage—particularly for inference jobs with predictable utilization.

### Effective cost is falling through commitments and utilization

Reservation economics are increasingly decisive. One-year commitments reduce median GPU pricing by about 21%, while three-year commitments cut it by approximately 48% versus on-demand rates. [1] Google’s three-year H100 commitment was listed at $4.86 per GPU-hour, compared with an $11.06 on-demand rate; its H200 equivalent was $4.65 versus $10.60. [4] 

Spot pricing can be dramatically lower—up to 91% below on-demand in some Google configurations—but availability and interruption risk make it unsuitable as the sole basis for distributed training capacity. [4] The next quarters should therefore see more hybrid scheduling: committed capacity for critical training, spot for checkpointable jobs, and neocloud overflow for inference.

...

Expect advertised hyperscaler GPU rates to remain sticky through the next two quarters, with selective increases where supply is tight—AWS raised several U.S. GPU configurations by about 15% in October after earlier 2026 increases. [9] Effective market pricing should nevertheless decline as neocloud supply expands and long-term discounts deepen.

results.title: Four EU clouds first read October 8-9, 2026: L4 from $0.27, H100 $9.01
highlights:
Between October 8 and October 9, 2026 we read four European GPU clouds for the first time: IONOS Cloud and STACKIT, which list in euros, and Hikube and Infomaniak, which list in Swiss francs. results.title: Why GPU prices spike during AI compute shortages | CloudPe Blog
highlights:
GPU prices spike when AI demand outpaces the memory, chip packaging, and power new GPUs need. In 2026, NVIDIA’s RTX PRO 6000 list price rose from $8,565 to $16,000, and B200 rentals jumped 79% in three months. Yet H100 rentals fell 64% to 75% from their 2024 peak.

...

Contract type matters too. Spot and on-demand rates track the market daily, while reserved contracts lock a price for a year or more. In 2026, reserved H100 prices rose about 40% while on-demand prices fell, because on-demand capacity was sold out.

## GPU prices in 2026

Cloud GPU rental prices are up 13% over 12 months across 21 models, with 16 rising and 5 falling. The GPU prices chart below shows the biggest moves. Rental figures are in US dollars per GPU-hour.

| GPU or price type | Earlier | Latest | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100, one-year contract | $1.70 (Oct 2025) | $2.35 (Mar 2026) | +38% |
| H100, on-demand median | 12 months ago | $3.57 (week of 12 Oct 2026) | +19% |
| B200 rental | 3 months ago | $8.01 (Sept 2026) | +79% |
| RTX PRO 6000 list price | $8,565 (Mar 2025) | $16,000 (Aug 2026) | +87% |

Note: Trackers measure different things, so the same GPU can show different prices. On 7 October, one list-price median put the H100 at $4.20, while trade-based indexes showed about $2.81 to $2.86.

...

## When do GPU prices spike, and when do they fall?

GPU prices spike when new demand lands before new supply, and they fall when supply catches up. The record from 2024 to 2026 shows four phases.

| Period | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| Early 2024 | H100 rentals peak at $8 to $10 an hour |
| Dec 2025 to Jan 2026 | H100 on-demand up 10% in four weeks, from $2.00 to $2.20 |
| Mar 2026 | One-year H100 contracts reach $2.35 |
| Jun 2026 | H100 eases to $2.01 to $2.53 as Blackwell supply ramps |
| 1 Oct 2026 | Nebius raises H100 on-demand from $3.85 to $4.50 |

From the above table reading, each fall followed new supply, and each rise followed a new kind of demand or a new bottleneck. The shortage has moved from GPUs to memory and power, which is why spikes keep returning.
